body.p: This listing of claims will replace all prior versions and listings of claims in theapplication:

br.br:
Claim 1. (Currently Amended): A leverage-reducing landing gear system
for an aircraft, said aircraft having a front, a rear, a top, a bottom, and a central verticallongitudinal plane perpendicular to horizontal ground and extending from said front tosaid rear, said aircraft having an airframe and landing gear, said aircraft having a centerof gravity, said leverage-reducing landing gear system comprising:(a) said aircraft having a front, a rear, a top, a bottom, and a centralvertical longitudinal plane perpendicular to horizontal ground andextending from said front to said rear, said aircraft having anairframe and landing pear, said aircraft having a center of gravity;
(b) said landing gear including a first primary landing gear leg and a second primary landing gear leg, said first and second primary landing gear legs positioned on opposite sides of said central vertical longitudinal plane;
(c) (b) at least one first shock absorber functionally connected to said first primary landing gear leg, said at least one first shock absorber angled upward from said first primary landing gear leg toward said central vertical longitudinal plane at an angle less than 30 degrees; and
(d) (c) at least one second shock absorber functionally connected to said second primary landing gear leg, said at least one second shock absorber angled upward from said second primary landing
gear leg toward said central vertical longitudinal plane at an angle
less than 30 degrees.
Claim 2. (Original): The leverage-reducing landing gear system of . (Original): The leverage-reducing landing gear system of
said at least one first shock absorber angled upward from said first primary landing gear
leg toward said central vertical longitudinal plane at an angle less than 20 degrees, and
said at least one second shock absorber angled upward from said second primary
landing gear leg toward said central vertical longitudinal plane at an angle less than 20 degrees.
Claim 3. (Currently Amended): The leverage-reducing landing gear
system of claim 1, wherein angling said first and second at least one shock absorbers at angles less than 30 degrees allows for compact packaging of said leverage-reducinglanding gear system to at least reduces drag caused by externally-mounted landing gear while preserving interior cabin volume.
Claim 4. (Original): The leverage-reducing landing gear system of . (Original): The leverage-reducing landing gear system of
said first and second primary landing gear legs positioned between said center of
gravity and said front of said aircraft.
Claim 5. (Original): The leverage-reducing landing gear system of . (Original): The leverage-reducing landing gear system of
further comprising:(a) said at least one first shock absorber functionally connected to said
first primary landing gear leg via a first system of segments and connectors; and
(b) said at least one second shock absorber functionally connected to said second primary landing gear leg via a system of segments and connectors.
Claim 6. (Original): The leverage-reducing landing gear system of . (Original): The leverage-reducing landing gear system of
further comprising:(a) said first primary landing gear leg pivotably connected to said
airframe by a first leg pivot point and rotatably connected to a first leg-to-arm linkage via a first leg-linkage rotator, said first leg-to-arm linkage rotatably connected to a first leverage-reducing arm via a first arm-linkage rotator, said first leverage-reducing arm pivotably connected to said airframe via a first arm pivot point and rotatably connected to said at least one first shock absorber via a first arm- shock rotator; and
(b) said second primary landing gear leg pivotably connected to said airframe by a second leg pivot point and rotatably connected to a second leg-to-arm linkage via a second leg-linkage rotator, said second leg-to-arm linkage rotatably connected to a second leverage-reducing arm via a second arm-linkage rotator, said second leverage-reducing arm pivotably connected to said airframe via a second arm pivot point and rotatably connected to said at least one second shock absorber via a second arm-shock rotator.
Claim 7. (Original): The leverage-reducing landing gear system of . (Original): The leverage-reducing landing gear system of
being an energy-absorbing, damped landing gear system.
Claim 8. (Original): The leverage-reducing landing gear system of . (Original): The leverage-reducing landing gear system of
said airframe defining a fuselage, one end of each of said first and second primary
landing gear legs positioned within said fuselage.
Claim 9. (Original): The leverage-reducing landing gear system of . (Original): The leverage-reducing landing gear system of
said landing gear including tires.
Claim 10. (Currently Amended): The leverage-reducing landing gear
system of claim 1, further for use with a constant angle suspension landing pear system comprising:(a) said landing gear including a steerable tail wheel positioned toward
said rear of said aircraft and aligned with said central vertical longitudinal plane;
(b) at least one third shock absorber mounted between said airframe and said steerable tail wheel, said at least one third shock absorber above said steerable tail wheel; and
(c) at least one constant angle suspension mechanism mounted between said airframe and said steerable tail wheel, said at least one constant angle suspension mechanism being more toward said front of said aircraft than said steerable tail wheel.
Claim 11. (Withdrawn and Currently Amended): A constant angle
suspension landing gear system for an aircraft, said aircraft having a front, a rear, a top,
a bottom, and a central vertical longitudinal plane perpendicular to horizontal ground
and extending from said front to said rear, said aircraft having an airframe and landinggear, said aircraft having a center of gravity, said constant angle suspension landing gear system comprising:(a) said aircraft having a front, a rear, a top, a bottom, and a centralvertical longitudinal plane perpendicular to horizontal ground andextending from said front to said rear, said aircraft having anairframe and landing pear, said aircraft having a center of gravity;
(b) said landing gear including a castered tire positioned to align with said central vertical longitudinal plane;
(c) (b) at least one secondary shock absorber mounted between said airframe and said castered tire; and
(d) (c) at least one constant angle suspension mechanism mounted between said airframe and said castered tire, said at least one constant angle suspension mechanism being more toward said front of said aircraft than said castered tire.
Claim 12. (Withdrawn): The constant angle suspension landing gear
system of claim 11, said at least one constant angle suspension mechanism being a four-bar suspension mechanism.
Claim 13. (Withdrawn): The constant angle suspension landing gear
system of claim 11, said castered tire positioned between said center of gravity and said rear of said aircraft.

system of claim 11, said at least one constant angle suspension mechanism being a four-bar suspension mechanism further comprising:(a) at least one upper tail wheel control arm;
(b) at least one lower tail wheel control arm;
(c) at least one fuselage mount, said at least one fuselage mount

and

(b) said fuselage mount rotatably mounting said constant angle
suspension mechanism to said airframe;
(c) said shock absorber mount mounting said at least one secondary shock absorber to said aircraft; and

angle suspension mechanism.

said at least one caster mount rotatably mounting said at
least one upper tail wheel control arm and said at least one
lower tail wheel control arm to said at least one fuselage
mount.

system of claim 11, further comprising:(a) a fuselage mount, a shock absorber mount, and a caster mount;
(b) said fuselage mount rotatably mounting said constant angle
suspension mechanism to said airframe;
(c) said shock absorber mount rotatably mounting said at least one secondary shock absorber to said aircraft; and
(d) said caster mount forming a junction between said castered tire,said at least one secondary shock absorber, and said constant

Claim 18. (Withdrawn and Currently Amended): The constant angle
suspension landing gear system of claim 11, further comprising for use with a leverage- reducing landing gear system comprising:(a) said landing gear including a first primary landing gear leg and a
second primary landing gear leg, said first and second primary landing gear legs positioned on opposite sides of said central vertical longitudinal plane;
(b) at least one first shock absorber functionally connected to said first primary landing gear leg, said at least one first shock absorber angled upward from said first primary landing gear leg toward said central vertical longitudinal plane at an angle less than 30 degrees;

Claim 19. (Currently Amended): A landing gear system for an aircraft,
said aircraft having a front, a rear, a top, a bottom, and a central vertical longitudinal
plane perpendicular to horizontal ground and extending from said front to said rear, saidaircraft having an airframe and landing gear, said aircraft having a center of gravity, said landing gear system comprising:(a) said aircraft having a front, a rear, a top, a bottom, and a centralvertical longitudinal plane perpendicular to horizontal ground andextending from said front to said rear, said aircraft having anairframe and landing pear, said aircraft having a center of gravity;
(b) a leverage-reducing landing gear system for an aircraft, comprising:(i) said landing gear including a first primary landing gear leg
and a second primary landing gear leg, said first and second primary landing gear legs positioned on opposite sides of said central vertical longitudinal plane;
(ii) at least one first shock absorber functionally connected to said first primary landing gear leg, said at least one first shock absorber angled upward from said first primary landing gear leg toward said central vertical longitudinal plane at an angle less than 30 degrees; and
(iii) at least one second shock absorber functionally connected
to said second primary landing gear leg, said at least one second shock absorber angled upward from said second primary landing gear leg toward said central vertical longitudinal plane at an angle less than 30 degrees; and
(c) (b) a constant angle suspension landing gear system for an aircraft, comprising:
(i) said landing gear including secondary landing pear including a castered tire positioned to align with said central vertical longitudinal plane;
(ii) at least one secondary shock absorber mounted between said airframe and said castered tire; and
(iii) at least one constant angle suspension mechanism mounted between said airframe and said castered tire, said at least one constant angle suspension mechanism being more toward said front of said aircraft than said castered tire;
(d) wherein said landing pear is fixed landing pear.
